statement: Chameleons can change the color of their skin.
fact: They really can change color. The change may help with communication, temperature control, or showing stress—not just hiding from predators.

vocab.definition: colors or patterns that help an animal blend into its surroundings

statement: A platypus is a mammal, even though it lays eggs.
fact: Platypuses are monotremes: rare mammals that lay eggs. Their mothers also produce milk for their young.

vocab.definition: a warm-blooded animal whose young drink milk from their mother

statement: Ostriches can fly for short distances when they run fast enough.
fact: Ostriches cannot fly, but no bird can run faster on land. Their powerful legs are built for speed and defense.

vocab.definition: unable to fly

statement: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have lived on Earth.
fact: Blue whales can reach about 110 feet and 330,000 pounds. They are larger than any known dinosaur.

vocab.definition: extremely large

statement: The cheetah is the fastest animal on land.
fact: A cheetah can sprint at roughly 60–70 miles per hour, but it can hold that top speed for only a short distance.

vocab.definition: to run at top speed for a short time

statement: A whale shark is a type of whale.
fact: Despite its name and huge size, the whale shark is a fish. It is the largest fish in the world.

vocab.definition: a group of living things of the same kind

statement: Dolphins are fish because they live in the ocean.
fact: Dolphins are mammals. They breathe air with lungs, are warm-blooded, and feed milk to their young.

vocab.definition: connected with the sea or ocean

statement: Elephants are the largest living animals on land.
fact: African elephants are the biggest land mammals. An adult male can weigh several tonnes.

vocab.definition: living or happening on land

statement: A camel stores water inside its hump.
fact: A camel's hump stores fat, not water. The body can use that fat for energy when food is scarce.

vocab.definition: difficult to find or available only in small amounts

statement: Bats are birds with fur instead of feathers.
fact: Bats are mammals, and they are the only mammals capable of true powered flight.

vocab.definition: active mainly during the night

statement: An octopus has three hearts.
fact: Two hearts move blood through the gills, while a third pumps oxygen-rich blood around the rest of the body.

vocab.definition: the movement of blood around a body

statement: An owl can turn its head all the way around in a full circle.
fact: Most owls can turn their heads up to about 270 degrees, which is impressive but not a full 360-degree circle.

vocab.definition: to turn around a central point

statement: A narwhal's long tusk is actually a tooth.
fact: The famous spiral tusk is a specialized tooth with nerves that connect its inner core to the outside.

vocab.definition: a very long tooth that grows outside an animal's mouth

statement: The Arctic tern makes the longest migration of any bird.
fact: Arctic terns travel between far northern breeding grounds and waters near Antarctica, following summer around the planet.

vocab.definition: regular seasonal travel from one region to another

statement: Electric eels can produce electricity to hunt and defend themselves.
fact: Special electric organs let these fish produce strong shocks. They can use weaker signals to sense their surroundings too.

vocab.definition: an action or ability used for protection

statement: An axolotl can regrow a lost limb.
fact: Axolotls can rebuild skin, bone, muscle, and other tissues to form a new limb, which makes them important to scientists.

vocab.definition: to grow again after being damaged or lost

statement: Hummingbirds can fly backward.
fact: Their unusual wing motion lets hummingbirds hover, fly backward, and even fly upside down for short moments.

vocab.definition: to stay in one place in the air

statement: A dolphin can rest one half of its brain while the other half stays awake.
fact: This is called unihemispheric sleep. The awake half helps the dolphin surface to breathe and stay aware of danger.

vocab.definition: one half of a sphere or, here, one half of the brain

statement: Sea otters use rocks as tools to open hard-shelled food.
fact: Sea otters commonly use rocks or other hard objects to break open snails, crabs, and abalones.

vocab.definition: an object used to help perform a task

statement: Cheetahs can roar as loudly as lions.
fact: Cheetahs do not roar. They communicate with purrs, chirps, barks, growls, hisses, and other sounds.

vocab.definition: a sound made with the voice to communicate

statement: In a hunting dive, a peregrine falcon can move faster than a cheetah runs.
fact: A diving peregrine can exceed 230 miles per hour, making it the fastest animal overall. The cheetah keeps the land-speed title.

vocab.definition: a falcon's very fast dive toward prey

statement: The world's smallest bird weighs less than many coins.
fact: Cuba's bee hummingbird weighs about 1.95 grams. It is lighter than a U.S. penny.

vocab.definition: very small; a tiny version of something

statement: Chameleons change color only to match the background and hide.
fact: Camouflage is only part of the story. Color changes can communicate mood, display health, respond to temperature, or signal stress.

vocab.definition: an action, sound, or color that communicates information

statement: The orca, often called a killer whale, is actually the largest member of the dolphin family.
fact: Common names can be confusing: orcas belong to the oceanic dolphin family, Delphinidae.

vocab.definition: the act of arranging living things into scientific groups

statement: The world's biggest fish mainly eats tiny organisms such as plankton.
fact: Whale sharks strain plankton, small schooling fish, and squid from the water. Their huge size does not make them hunters of large prey.

vocab.definition: an animal that removes tiny food from water as it feeds

statement: Flamingos are born with bright pink feathers.
fact: Flamingo chicks have gray down. Their pink or red color develops from carotenoid pigments in algae and small crustaceans they eat.

vocab.definition: a natural substance that gives color to plants or animals

statement: An echidna is a mammal that lays an egg.
fact: Echidnas and platypuses are monotremes. Female echidnas usually lay one leathery egg and carry it in a pouch.

vocab.definition: to keep an egg warm while the young animal develops

statement: Every polar bear hibernates through the Arctic winter.
fact: Polar bears generally stay active through winter. Pregnant females are the ones that spend winter in maternity dens.

vocab.definition: to spend winter in a deep resting state that saves energy

statement: A blue whale's heart can weigh more than 1,000 pounds (about 450 kilograms).
fact: NOAA reports that a blue whale heart can weigh more than an average dairy cow. The whale's enormous body needs an enormous pump.

vocab.definition: a body part with a special job, such as the heart or lungs

statement: Octopus blood is red, just like human blood.
fact: Octopus blood is blue because it uses a copper-based molecule called hemocyanin to carry oxygen.

vocab.definition: a gas that animals need for respiration and energy
